title: Disruption of biological tissues for GAG disaccharide prep
author: H Davies-Strickleton
materials: Bead homogenisation via Qiagen TissueLyser II Detailed protocols are provided in the supplier user manual . Guidelines are provided in this section

Amount of tissue required for GAG disaccharide analysis by HILIC-MS/MS For comprehensive characterisation of GAG disaccharides (in order to detect as many of the disaccharides as possible), the recommended amount of tissue is: ≥ 5 mg tissue For identification of the most abundant disaccharides (in order to compare relative GAG disaccharide levels across samples), the recommended amount of tissue is: ≥ 0.5 mg tissue* * The amounts of tissue given here are initial guidelines based on observations during method development. Lower amounts of tissue are likely to provide data, but the the lower limit of tissue required has not been fully determined, and will depend on tissue type. Disruption of tissue < 5 mg This section covers tissue that is ~ 5 mg or less. Here, homogenisation of the tissue is performed by bead homogenisation with a Qiagen TissueLyser II. Other forms of homogenisation may be possible but have not been tested at the time of publication of this protocol. For samples > 5 mg see preceding sections in this protocol. Safety Tissue should be handled in a class II microbiological safety cabinet to protect the user from any risk of infectious agents.
Option for generating tissue homogenates - Bead homogenisation via Qiagen TissueLyser II Detailed protocols are provided in the supplier user manual . Guidelines are provided in this section.

Amount of FFPE tissue required for GAG disaccharide analysis by HILIC-MS/MS The amount of tissue per FFPE block varies greatly with sample type (e.g. population differences, organ type (e.g. liver vs brain) and species (e.g. mouse vs human)). At the time of publication of this protocol, comprehensive characterisation of GAG disaccharides has been demonstrated from the following amounts of FFPE material: 3 x 25 μm FFPE scrolls of mouse kidney per sample 1 x 10 μm FFPE scroll of human kidney biopsy Disruption of tissue FFPE scrolls Here, tissue is liberated from FFPE scrolls by bead homogenisation with a Qiagen TissueLyser II, decrosslinked by incubation at 98 oC and homogenised by further bead homogenisation. Alternative techniques for the liberation of tissue homogenates from FFPE scrolls techniques may be possible but have not been tested at the time of publication of this protocol. Normalisation for relative quantification of GAGs per FFPE sample At the time of publication of this protocol, normalisation for FFPE scrolls is under optimisation. Options include: Estimation of tissue area per sample by calculation of tissue cross-sectional areas from FFPE blocks (FFPE scrolls thickness should be fixed for all samples to be compared); Calculation of protein amount in tissue after liberation and homogenisation from FFPE sections using Bicinchoninic Acid (BCA) Assay. Note: the amount of tissue required for the BCA assay may be greater than the amount required for GAG analysis by HILIC MS/MS, therefore a greater number of FFPE scrolls might be required if this normalisation approach is selected. Safety During homogenisation steps, avoid opening tubes outside a class II microbiological safety cabinet to protect the user from any risk of aerosolised infectious agents.

steps.title: Determine required sample amount
steps.instruction: Based on analysis goals, collect ≥5 mg tissue for comprehensive GAG profiling or ≥0.5 mg for abundant disaccharides; for cells collect 1 × 10⁶ cells for comprehensive or >5 × 10⁴ cells for abundant CS/DS/HA or HS. Record the amount for later normalisation.

steps.title: Collect and wash cells
steps.instruction: Harvest the required number of cells, pellet by centrifugation at 300 × g for 3 min, discard media, resuspend in PBS, repeat PBS wash twice, and after the final wash remove most liquid.

substeps.instruction: Repeat wash two more times (centrifuge 300 × g, 3 min each).
After the last wash, pipette off excess PBS, leaving a minimal volume.

steps.title: Wash stainless steel beads
steps.instruction: Rinse 5 mm stainless steel beads (Qiagen 69989) in water, then store them in 70 % ethanol until use.

steps.title: Optional protein assay
steps.instruction: Measure protein concentration of the cell pellet (e.g., BCA assay) for later normalisation of GAG data.

steps.title: Optional repeat homogenisation
steps.instruction: If tissue remains, add 200 μL PBS, homogenise 2 × 30 s at 30 Hz, heat at 98 °C for 30 min, centrifuge 300 × g for 1 min, and combine the resulting homogenate with the first to obtain a total of 400 μL. Apply the same procedure to all samples in the batch.

steps.title: Centrifuge homogenate and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 300 × g for 1 min; wax pellets stick to tube walls while tissue remains in PBS. Pipette the PBS up and down to recover any sedimented tissue and transfer the homogenate to a fresh microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Homogenise and decrosslink tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenise at 30 Hz for 2 × 30 s, then heat at 98 °C for 30 min, inverting or vortexing briefly halfway through (do not open lids).

steps.title: Section FFPE block
steps.instruction: Use a microtome to cut the FFPE block into scrolls: 1 × 25 μm and 3 × 10 μm sections (or as optimised), and collect the required number into a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Weigh tissue and record weight
steps.instruction: Weigh the tissue or sections. For 100‑300 mg samples record the weight; if >300 mg, dissect to 100‑300 mg pieces and record each weight. For 5‑100 mg samples record the weight as well.

steps.title: Prepare Covaris CryoPREP consumables
steps.instruction: Select consumables based on tissue mass: • 100‑300 mg: tissueTUBE TT1 Extra Thick (Covaris 520007), TT1‑milliTUBE adapter (520142), milliTUBE 2 mL (520132), insertion tool (500159). • 5‑100 mg: tissueTUBE TT05 (520071), milliTUBE 1 mL (520128). Place the weighed tissue into the appropriate tissueTUBE.

steps.title: Assemble CryoPREP and pulverise
steps.instruction: Assemble the tissueTUBE onto the milliTUBE using the adapter, insert the assembly into the Insertion Tool, briefly submerge the tissueTUBE in liquid nitrogen, place the assembly on the CryoPREP, close the lid, choose the appropriate impact level, press Activate, and repeat activation if pulverisation is insufficient.

steps.title: Recover powdered tissue
steps.instruction: After pulverisation, hold the assembly, dip the tissueTUBE briefly in liquid nitrogen, roll the tube over a 50 mL Duran bottle to break clumps, invert the tissueTUBE over the milliTUBE and flick to transfer the powder into the milliTUBE.

steps.title: Optional soluble homogenate preparation
steps.instruction: For soluble homogenate only, centrifuge the disrupted tissue at 10 000 rpm for 10 min and collect the supernatant; otherwise retain both soluble and insoluble material.

steps.title: Add PBS to tube
steps.instruction: Add PBS to each tube: 100‑400 μL for tissue samples or 100‑200 μL for cell samples. Volume may be optimised per sample type.

steps.title: Add stainless steel bead and load TissueLyser
steps.instruction: Add one 5 mm stainless steel bead (Qiagen 69989) to each 2 mL tube, place tubes in the TissueLyser II adapter (up to 24 tubes), balance the adapters, attach lids and clamp the adapter onto the TissueLyser.

steps.title: Homogenise on TissueLyser
steps.instruction: Homogenise at 30 Hz for 4 × 30 s (or 2 × 30 s for earlier optional step). Pause as needed; volume can be optimised per tissue type.

steps.title: Transfer homogenate and clean bead
steps.instruction: Transfer the homogenate to a fresh tube, leaving the stainless steel bead behind. Wash the bead in 70 % ethanol then water, and store the bead in 70 % ethanol for reuse.

steps.title: Optional photograph FFPE block
steps.instruction: Photograph the FFPE block next to a ruler to estimate tissue area; the area can later be used for normalisation of GAG amounts.

steps.title: Store samples before GAG preparation
steps.instruction: Store processed samples at –80 °C (cell pellets may be stored at –20 °C) until GAG disaccharide preparation. Storage conditions may require optimisation for each sample type.
